title: Blood Flow Restriction Training in Patients With Lower Extremity Fractures
official: Blood Flow Restriction Training Versus Traditional Rehab in Patients With Lower Extremity Fractures: Effect on Fracture Healing, Muscle Strength and Girth, and Return to Function
summary: This study will look at the effect of using a blood flow restriction device during low load strengthening exercises on patients with tibial shaft fractures, compared to patients performing exercise without the device. The study will compare muscle strength, muscle size, fracture healing, and return to normal function between the two groups.

interventions.name: Blood Flow Restriction with low load exercise

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adult with closed tibial shaft fracture
* Ability to begin physical therapy treatment within 2 weeks post-operatively

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of osteoporosis or osteopenia
* Impaired circulation in the limb
* Active deep vein thrombosis
* Clotting disorders or other elevated risk of embolism
* Sickle cell anemia
* Infection in extremity
* Renal compromise
* Severe uncontrolled hypertension (SBP\>180)
* Lymphedema
* Under age 18
* Pregnancy
* Prisoner
